subject: physical-education

location.unitTitle: Adapted and Lifelong Inclusive Activity Design
location.courseTitle: Lifelong Wellness and Independent Training Capstone

standardsMappingAuthority.note: Standards remain governed by the bound production package.

instructions: Complete the safe activity or accessible equivalent and document the requested performance evidence.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing trouble, unsafe conditions, or missing adult supervision.

learnerTasks.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of activity across a lifespan and how demands change in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe adapting an activity after injury, illness, or changed capability using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply adapted sport and inclusive formats as durable options in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving designing activity for a group with mixed ages and abilities; correct it and explain why.
Connect the social side: finding people to be active with as an adult with letting go of an activity without letting go of activity and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Take one activity the learner values and produce three adapted versions of it — for reduced mobility, for very limited time, and for a mixed-age group — with the reasoning for each.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

learnerSuccessCriteria: Provide evidence that meets the stated safe participation and self-management criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated skill cues or movement quality criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated tactical or training reasoning criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated self-assessment and revision criterion.
accommodations: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.

provenance.unitObjective: How can the learner demonstrate the goals of Adapted and Lifelong Inclusive Activity Design?
